inputs.root_cause: XLIFF-SEG-001's 4 obligations all shared one identical, generic-ish citation (the same 3 production_namespace.py tests already reused across dozens of other xliff obligations). Investigated each rule_text against the real segmentation.py/validator.py/document.py source directly.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 1 obligation closed via cross-file citation to an existing, real, previously-uncited test (proving source/target content carrying). 1 obligation closed with 2 new tests for a genuine, previously-unenforced structural rule (unit must contain at least one segment/ignorable -- the 'exactly one source, at most one target' half is a structural guarantee of the Segment dataclass shape, not a runtime check). 2 obligations closed via a new, previously-unbuilt feature: srcLang/trgLang xml:lang compatibility validation, version-aware (XLIFF 2.0 exact-only, XLIFF 2.1 exact-or-more-specific per the F4T Schematron), with 5 new tests.

execution_steps: 1. Read all 4 obligations' exact rule_text. Grepped tests/python/xliff for any file already touching split_segment/join_segments/SegmentMapping and found only the shared, generic production_namespace.py citation -- but reading that file in full (not just the 3 cited test names) surfaced two real, dedicated, previously-uncited tests in the SAME file: test_segment_split_join_reports_mapping_and_preserves_inline_content and test_segment_split_rejects_boundary_that_orphans_a_spanning_code. Confirmed these directly and precisely prove SAL-XLIFF-OBL-5BB18B34B798FCC4's source/target content-carrying claim; re-cited using the already-existing XLIFF-SEGMENT-SPLIT-JOIN-SELECTOR-PROOF execution evidence entry (which already covers 2 other obligations with the same real test evidence) rather than minting a duplicate entry.

2. Read model/document.py's Segment and Unit dataclasses directly: Segment has exactly one source field and one optional target field, so 'exactly one source, at most one target' is a structural type-system guarantee -- there is no code path that could construct a Segment with more than one of either, so this half needs no runtime test. Grepped validator.py and confirmed NOTHING enforces 'a unit contains at least one segment or ignorable child' -- a zero-segment Unit passed validate() silently. Added a new xliff.unit.segment.required diagnostic and 2 new tests (positive: segment or ignorable accepted; negative: empty unit refused).

3. Grepped validator.py and model/document.py for any xml:lang / srcLang / trgLang compatibility logic and found none beyond a bare 'srcLang is required' presence check -- confirmed via direct source reading (GAP-008) that language-tag compatibility validation genuinely does not exist. Found the existing xml:lang Clark-notation constant already defined in model/text_editing.py and reused the same convention. Implemented _language_compatible(enclosing, declared, exact_only) -- exact equality always accepted; a more-specific tag (e.g. declared 'en-US' under enclosing 'en') additionally accepted unless exact_only, matching the rule_text's explicit XLIFF 2.0 (exact-only) vs XLIFF 2.1 (exact-or-more-specific, per the normative F4T Schematron) distinction. Wired this into validate() for both segment source xml:lang (against document.source_language) and segment target xml:lang (against document.target_language, skipped when no target language is declared).

4. Verified all 4 new/changed behaviors interactively (empty unit rejected; 2.1 more-specific source lang accepted; 2.0 same tag rejected; unrelated lang rejected) before writing any formal test, then wrote 9 tests in a new file, test_obligation_segment_structure_and_language.py, covering both the structure check and the language-compatibility check (source and target, both XLIFF versions, case-insensitivity, and the no-declared-target-language skip case).

5. Ran ruff and mypy on the one changed source file (clean), the new test file alone (9 passed), and the full xliff suite (339 passed, unchanged from before -- confirming the new validator checks do not false-positive against any existing fixture) before writing any evidence claim. Ran the skills-first resolve/manifest/receipt/closeout sequence since src/ was touched, then patched the evidence YAML and ran the reconciler.
